assessment.nobel_worthiness: The observation of a new boson consistent with the Standard Model Higgs particle is an original, decisive experimental discovery that completed the Standard Model and opened a measurement programme on the scalar sector. The theory was recognised in 2013, but the experimental discovery has not been; this is exactly the discovery-by-experiment the prize is meant for.
assessment.attribution: The discovery rests on two independent collaborations of thousands, so credit must go to the people who conceived and led the experiments. Della Negra and Jenni were founding proposers and leaders of CMS and ATLAS respectively, and Gianotti led ATLAS at the time of the announcement. Virdee is an equally strong CMS figure, so a three-person slate leaves one credible name out and balances CMS and ATLAS only imperfectly.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed independently by two experiments and by years of coupling measurements at the LHC. The interpretation is stable, and recognition is not premature.
uncertainties: Which three of the four credited names best represent the two collaborations is a judgement; CMS has Della Negra and Virdee but only one can be chosen alongside the two ATLAS names, or the reverse.
I rely on my own knowledge of the roles of the individuals and have not independently verified the details of each person's leadership role and timing.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Katori's magic-wavelength optical lattice proposal and Ye's demonstration of its precision turned optical clocks into the most accurate measurement devices ever built. It is a new tool that opens a door: tests of fundamental constants, relativistic geodesy and a candidate redefinition of the second.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the original idea (2003) and made the first demonstrations; Ye took it to the extreme accuracy and stability regime. The two-person configuration is clean. The 2005 prize covered the frequency comb, not the clock itself, so there is no overlap.
assessment.maturity: Multiple groups have independent realisations, and the clocks are at the 10^-18 level and in international comparison campaigns. Mature and timely.
uncertainties: Single-ion optical clocks (Wineland's 2012 prize) are a neighbouring contribution, and the committee would need to be comfortable about the division of credit between ion and lattice clocks.
Others (for example Lemonde, Schmidt, Hollberg) played roles in the optical clock history that I cannot fully rank from the supplied text.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The theoretical prediction of the quantum spin Hall effect and the Z2 invariant, followed by the experimental observation in HgTe quantum wells, created the field of topological insulators. It is conceptually original, with a clear and decisive experimental verification.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele introduced the Z2 classification and the quantum spin Hall idea in graphene. The original observation of the edge-channel conduction was by Molenkamp's group in HgTe, building on the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal. The latter is not on the supplied credit list, and I would want the committee to examine whether it is fair to omit them.
assessment.maturity: Many independent experimental confirmations across materials (HgTe, Bi2Se3 and others) and robust theory two decades later. Timely and no longer premature.
uncertainties: The role of Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang (HgTe proposal), and of Fu, Kane and Mele (3D topological insulators), complicates the three-person allocation.
I cannot verify the priority claims against the original papers in this stage.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The 2008 discovery of superconductivity at 26 K in fluorine-doped LaFeAsO opened an entire second family of high-temperature superconductors beyond the cuprates. This is an original materials discovery, clearly experimental, with broad impact on correlated-electron physics.
assessment.attribution: The original report came from Hosono's group at Tokyo Institute of Technology (Kamihara et al.). The candidate is a single credited person, which is clean, though the subsequent rapid rise in Tc to 55 K by Chinese groups was a follow-on and should not be confused with the original discovery.
assessment.maturity: Rapid independent confirmation by many laboratories, large literature, and a stable understanding of the phase diagram. The microscopic pairing mechanism remains unsettled, which is a caution but not a barrier, since the prize is for the discovery.
uncertainties: The pairing mechanism is not settled, so the physical interpretation of the discovery remains open.
Whether a single laureate adequately represents the credit (collaborators in the original paper) is something the committee should check against the record.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Aberration-corrected electron optics broke the long-standing resolution limit of the electron microscope and made sub-angstrom imaging and spectroscopy of atoms routine in materials science. It is a new instrument that opened a door for seeing atomic structure, and its impact across materials science is large.
assessment.attribution: Rose proposed the corrector design, Haider and collaborators built the hexapole corrector for the TEM, and Urban led the first demonstration of its benefit in a working microscope for materials. The three names fit a fair split between theory of the optics, construction and application. The supplied text does not rule on the roles of Krivanek (STEM correctors) and others, who deserve a close look.
assessment.maturity: Widely adopted worldwide, independently verified, and the field is well established. Already honoured by the Wolf and Kavli prizes, which suggests it is ripe.
uncertainties: I work in electron microscopy and know this field closely, so my judgement may be biased in either direction; the committee should weigh my ranking accordingly.
The credit for the aberration-corrected STEM (Krivanek, Dellby and colleagues, and Batson) is not in the credited list, which may weaken the fairness of the proposed configuration.
The Nobel Prize in Chemistry 2017 and Physics 1986 have previously recognised electron microscopy, so the committee will ask whether this is a distinct step.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The detection of a diffuse flux of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos in a cubic-kilometre Antarctic ice detector opened neutrino astronomy at energies far beyond earlier sources. This is a new instrument that opened a new window, with later source identifications (the blazar TXS 0506+056 and the Seyfert galaxy NGC 1068) and a Galactic-plane detection.
assessment.attribution: IceCube is a large collaboration, but Halzen was the principal driving figure of the concept and the project, and Karle is credited for the detector-construction and ice-physics side. The supplied credit list is short, and I would want more evidence on whether other early leaders (for example in AMANDA or in the IceCube project office) should be included.
assessment.maturity: The diffuse flux has been confirmed in several analyses and by independent detector channels, and source associations at the multi-sigma level followed. The astrophysical origin of the bulk of the flux is not yet resolved, but the discovery itself is secure.
uncertainties: The origin of the diffuse neutrino flux is unresolved, so the physics follow-up may still change the story.
A large collaboration makes a two- or three-person attribution difficult, and the committee must verify who made the decisive contributions.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical coherence tomography is an instrument invention that applies low-coherence interferometry to image tissue in vivo at micrometre resolution, and it is now standard in ophthalmology. The prize is explicitly for invention and benefit to humanity, and OCT is a clear example, though its scientific novelty lies more in application of known interferometry than in new physics.
assessment.attribution: The 1991 Science paper by Huang, Swanson, Fujimoto and colleagues is the commonly cited origin. There is a prior history of low-coherence interferometry in biology and ophthalmology (for example Fercher and colleagues in Vienna), so the priority of the invention is not entirely clean, and I would want the historical record examined in detail.
assessment.maturity: Independent adoption worldwide and decades of clinical use. Timely, and arguably overdue if the committee considers it within physics.
uncertainties: Priority relative to earlier low-coherence interferometry work (Fercher, Hitzenberger and others) is a real concern for 'the original experiment' principle.
Whether the invention is considered within physics, and whether Fujimoto, Huang and Swanson are the right trio, would need discussion.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Metal-halide perovskites went from a 3.8 percent dye-sensitised-style solar cell to certified efficiencies above 25 percent within about a decade, an unusually rapid and verified development with large implications for photovoltaics and for optoelectronic materials physics.
assessment.attribution: Miyasaka first reported the perovskite sensitised cell in 2009; Park and Snaith made the key advances to solid-state, efficient devices in 2011 and 2012. The credit is plausible as a three-person group, but others (for example Grätzel, Kanatzidis, Mitzi on earlier perovskite semiconductors) have contributions that the committee must weigh.
assessment.maturity: Efficiency is independently verified in many laboratories, but long-term operational stability and lead toxicity are open, and the field may be too young for a prize aimed at a settled discovery.
uncertainties: Stability of devices over product lifetimes is not established, so the technological impact is not yet proven.
The topic sits at the border of physics and chemistry, and credit disputes over the earliest solid-state devices are unresolved.
